V.rationale: Visa's fundamental health and trajectory are strong: revenue grew +17.1% YoY to $11.23B in Q2 FY2026, net income expanded +31.5% YoY to $6.02B, and operating margin reached 64.4% on a single-quarter basis (trailing 61.1%). ROE at 62.4% is elite. The franchise is durable — 60% US card-network market share, asset-light model, near-zero marginal cost, and value-added services growing 27% YoY at 30% of revenue. However, two concerns cap the score below +0.5: (1) OCF collapsed to $3.01B in Q2 FY2026, down -55.6% QoQ and -35.9% YoY, creating genuine uncertainty about cash-generation quality despite record net income; and (2) key valuation metrics (PE, EV/EBIT, FCF yield) are unavailable, preventing confirmation that the market hasn't already priced in this strong trajectory — the stock at $324.95 is -13.5% below its 365-day high of $375.51 despite surging earnings, suggesting the market may be discounting OCF weakness or macro headwinds (oil at $92.65, rising rates). On the positive side, the stock appears to have underperformed its fundamental improvement, and the $20B buyback authorization (April 2026) plus potential China market access via Trump advocacy provide modest near-term catalysts. Berkshire's complete exit is a negative signal but appears portfolio-specific rather than thesis-driven. Regulatory risk (CCCA) remains an overhang but legislative progress has stalled. Net: high-quality compounder with excellent trajectory, but OCF concern and valuation opacity warrant a cautiously positive rather than strongly positive score.
key_factors: Revenue +17.1% YoY to $11.23B in Q2 FY2026, beating consensus of $10.74B by ~5%
Net income +31.5% YoY to $6.02B; adjusted EPS of $3.31 (+20% YoY), beating consensus by 7.1%
Operating margin 64.4% (single-quarter implied) / 61.1% (trailing); net margin 51.7%; ROE 62.4% — elite profitability
OCF collapsed to $3.01B in Q2 FY2026, down -55.6% QoQ and -35.9% YoY — disconnect from record net income flags working-capital headwind
Total equity declined from $38.78B to $35.66B; liability-to-equity rose to 1.67× from 1.50×
Stock at $324.95 is -13.5% below 365-day high of $375.51 despite strong earnings growth — market may be discounting OCF weakness or macro headwinds
Key valuation metrics (PE, EV/EBIT, FCF yield) unavailable — cannot confirm cheapness vs own history
Value-added services growing 27% YoY, now 30% of revenue — deepens moats and raises switching costs
Board authorized $20B multi-year share repurchase program in April 2026; TTM FCF ~$22.93B per external source
China market access opportunity via Trump advocacy (Benzinga, 2026-05-15) — incremental structural positive if realized
Berkshire Hathaway completely exited Visa in Q1 2026 — negative signal but appears portfolio-specific (16 positions exited)
Regulatory risk (CCCA) remains overhang but legislative attempts have stalled; practical execution barriers remain high
Oil at $92.65 (+30% in 90 days) is inflationary headwind to consumer spending and cross-border travel volumes
10-year Treasury yield at 4.45% (+40bp in 90 days) — rising rates increase discount rate on long-duration growth
